provenance.method: Algorithm parameters transcribed from the legacy NECB2020 water_heater_mixed_apply_efficiency and auto_size_shw_capacity, cross-verified against NECB 2020 Table 6.2.2.1 via the building-codes MCP (electric standby-loss formulas, gas-fired storage UEF ladders by tank volume + first-hour rating, Et >= 90% + SL formula for large equipment, oil rows). SHW demand data (peak flows, temperatures, schedules) lives in the openstudio-loads space-type records. Runtime never contacts the MCP.

Sentences (3)-(4) were machine-verified against the full article text (D-41) and are satisfied by clone; Part 6 minimums apply on top. autosize.note: pump head uses the OpenStudio constant-speed default (legacy default path); the legacy geometric mech-room piping-run head calculation is a documented future

efficiency.fhr_l_per_hr: 0.7 x tank_volume_litres + 151.0 (legacy first-hour-rating rule of thumb)

maguire_roberts.recovery_efficiency: eff + q_load x (uef - eff) / (24 x cap_btu_hr x uef)

part_load_curve.name: SWH-EFFFPLR-NECB2011
part_load_curve.derivation: 8.4.5.9.(2) writes a FUEL-RATIO curve: FHeatPLC = a + b(Qpl/Qdes) + c(Qpl/Qdes)^2, with Fuelpartload = Fueldesign x FHeatPLC. The EnergyPlus WaterHeater:Mixed 'Part Load Factor Curve Name' field is not that quantity — it is a DEGRADATION DIVISOR (fuel = Q_load / (eta x PLF)). The code curve therefore maps into the model field as PLF(x) = x / FHeatPLC(x), which is RATIONAL, not polynomial; the vendored cubic is its polynomial image and is probe-verified equivalent (max 0.98% over PLR 0.25-1.0, 1.47% down to PLR 0.10 — necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb, rake necb:curves). Vendoring the raw quadratic in the PLF field would invert the relation and overstate part-load fuel by +92% at half load and +253% at quarter load, and would double-count the a-term standby that E+ already carries as off-cycle parasitic fuel + tank UA. See D-53. The NECB2011-era NAME is retained deliberately for the legacy parity gate.
part_load_curve.applies_to_note: Fuel-fired only, and BOTH storage and instantaneous: the article is titled 'Fuel-Fired Service Water Heater' and governs 'the reference fuel-fired service water heater' without distinguishing storage from instantaneous. Electricity is outside the article's scope (D-53), not a silent skip.

articles.title: Service water heater performance (Table 6.2.2.1)
articles.how: electric storage (SL formulas), gas-fired storage (UEF ladders + Et>=90%/SL for large) and oil (via the gas path, legacy behavior) implemented on WaterHeaterMixed with Maguire-Roberts UA derivation; instantaneous rows (gas UEF 0.86 conservative / Et 0.94, oil Et 0.80, tankless zero UA) and storage heat-pump water heaters (WaterHeaterHeatPump build + code EF/UEF floor as rated COP) implemented
articles.gaps: pool-heater minimums IMPLEMENTED apply-when-present since D-63 (gas Et 82% / oil 78% / HP COP 4.0 floor set on heaters serving a SwimmingPoolIndoor; values from the printed rows hbix's table audit recovered — the extraction had LOST the solar/pool sections and the Volume of Tank column when D-41 ran its cross-check, so it could not see them; re-checked 2026-09-01, both sections are back and the column is present (the table now returns 57 rows, not 27) and the vendored minimums agree exactly; volume-binned values stand on their legacy-primary transcription). Solar-thermal SEF (>= 1.4 electric-aux / >= 0.9 gas-aux) is an equipment RATING with no EnergyPlus field: detected collectors get an audited determination, the physics stay cloned. No archetype exercises either class. HPWH uses the bounded pumped-condenser construction (upstream stratified-tank/EMS recipe not ported)

articles.title: Piping insulation
articles.gaps: the SHW plant carries no pipe objects and no pipe-run lengths, so insulation thickness cannot be checked against Table 6.2.3.1.; note also that pipe insulation IS costed (a fixed 10 ft/pump BOM line) while never being modelled, and the vendored Table 6.2.3.1. is known-damaged in the codes store (phantom/blank rows) so it would need PDF-verified re-vendoring first. Verified from drawings and on site.

articles.title: Service water temperature controls
articles.how: the storage tank is built with an automatic setpoint: a constant ScheduleRuleset at the sizing max temperature is installed as BOTH the loop SetpointManagerScheduled and the WaterHeaterMixed setpointTemperatureSchedule, with a 2 C deadband and Cycle control, so the tank is temperature-controlled and the setpoint is adjustable by editing one schedule

articles.title: Maintaining temperature (heat trace)
articles.gaps: no model object represents heat-trace temperature-maintenance controls; declared per run and verified from drawings

articles.title: Remote or booster heaters
articles.how: CHECKED against the sized demand: the fraction of total design flow whose target temperature exceeds 60 C is computed from the per-space demand before auto_size collapses it to one max_temp_c. Below 50% the sentence requires separate booster heaters for the hot portions, and a single-water-heater model is a SHOUTED finding; at or above 50%, or with no load above 60 C, the determination is audited as met or vacuous

articles.title: Hot service water fixture flow limits
articles.gaps: the model holds a per-AREA aggregate service-water demand with no fixture count, so a per-showerhead (7.6 L/min) or per-lavatory (5.7 private / 1.9 public L/min) rate cannot be derived from it; verified from the plumbing schedule

articles.title: Pools and hot tubs
articles.how: pool-heater minimum efficiencies ARE applied when a SwimmingPoolIndoor is present in the model (gas Et 82% / oil 78% / heat-pump COP 4.0, D-63, apply-when-present)
articles.gaps: the 6.2.7.1. shutoff device and pump/heater time switches are installed controls with no model object; 6.2.7.2. covers govern heated OUTDOOR pools and tubs, and EnergyPlus models INDOOR pools only, so that sentence is permanently outside model scope

articles.title: Service water heating loads representative of the building
articles.how: per-space WaterUseEquipment from the NECB space-type peak flows, target temperatures and NECB-<letter> SWH schedules (openstudio-loads data)

articles.title: Reference SWH identical to proposed (storage, power, energy type)

articles.how: apply_shw(fuel: 'HeatPump') builds an air-source HPWH; a reference generated from it keeps the air-source energy type by construction

articles.title: Remaining reference SWH sentences
articles.how: (3)/(4) verified against the full article text (retrieved via MCP 2026-07-28 after the ingestion fix): the umbrella's clone preserves the boiler-fed immersion coil's energy type ((3)) and the multi-energy capacity allocation and operating schedules identically — trivially matching the (4)(a) ratio (Note A-8.4.4.20.(4)(a) merely says how to determine it) and (4)(b) operational characteristics. Part 6 minimum efficiencies applied on top via apply_efficiency. (5) the 8.4.5.9.(2) FHeatPLC fuel part-load curve is applied to every fuel-fired reference water heater, storage AND instantaneous, via the documented PLF(x) = x / FHeatPLC(x) transform into the EnergyPlus part-load-factor field (probe-verified equivalent, max 0.98% over PLR 0.25-1.0; D-53). Electric water heaters carry NO such curve BY ARTICLE SCOPE, not by omission: 8.4.5.9 is titled 'Fuel-Fired Service Water Heater' and governs only the reference fuel-fired heater — there is no electric counterpart in 8.4.5 to apply.
articles.gaps: REFINED after machine-verification (D-41) and D-53: (3)/(4)/(6)/(7)/(8) are satisfied by clone and (5) is closed for every article-eligible heater. Remaining: (9) circulation-pump consolidation is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION for models this gem authors — necb/demand.rb builds exactly ONE PumpConstantSpeed per service water loop, so there is never a set of pumps to consolidate. It is unverified only for a FOREIGN proposed that arrives with several pumps on one SHW loop; such a model is cloned as-is, keeping identical W/(L/s) (energy-equivalent, topology differs). No consolidation pass is implemented because it would be unreachable code on every model this toolchain produces.
